content:
A slow-moving El Niño-fueled storm is bringing rounds of heavy rain to South Texas this weekend, with Laredo in the flood-threat zone and the greatest risk expected Sunday, according to Fox Weather and the National Weather Service.

Heavy rain began Saturday afternoon across parts of West, Central and South Texas, with the heaviest and most persistent rain expected Sunday afternoon through Sunday night, Fox Weather reported Saturday morning.

A Level 1 out of 4 flash flood risk covers a corridor from Laredo to Brownsville on Saturday, according to the FOX Forecast Center. The risk increases and shifts south on Sunday, with a broad Level 2 threat covering parts of the Hill Country and South Texas, including San Antonio.

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi issued a flood watch for portions of South Texas on Friday, November 6, at 8:17 p.m., in effect until noon Monday, November 9. Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible from Saturday afternoon through Monday morning, according to the weather service.

Widespread rainfall totals of up to 2 inches are expected from the Hill Country to the Gulf Coast through Tuesday, with localized amounts of up to 4 inches, as rain lingers into early next week.

Because there is very little atmospheric instability, rainfall rates should remain low, producing a steady, soaking rain rather than sudden, torrential downpours, the FOX Forecast Center said.

Residents should avoid driving through flooded roads and stay alert for rising water, especially in low-lying areas and near creeks and arroyos.

Update — November 8, 2026

The National Weather Service issued a flash flood warning for the Laredo area early Sunday morning, November 8, in effect from 5:04 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. CST, along with a flood advisory from 4:09 a.m. to 7:15 a.m. CST, according to the weather service’s alerts for Laredo. The flood watch for South Texas remains in effect until noon Monday, November 9.

Radar estimates put Laredo’s rainfall at about 0.89 inches over the previous 24 hours as of early Sunday morning. The Weather Prediction Center said Sunday that widespread totals of 3 to 6 inches are possible across South Texas, with the best chance of flash flooding late Sunday afternoon and evening into early Monday morning as rounds of heavy rain continue over eastern Webb County toward Corpus Christi.

As of early Sunday morning, no flooding, road closures, water rescues, or damage had been reported in the Laredo area. Webb Watch 956 will continue to watch for rainfall totals and any flooding reports through Monday.

Sources: Fox Weather, November 7, 2026; National Weather Service, Corpus Christi; National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center, November 8, 2026.

title: Flood Threat for Laredo as El Niño Storm Brings Heavy Rain Through the Weekend
